old: [When] the enemy and the conqueror, having combined, two enemies, two attackers of the other, are seizing the heel, he who seizes the heel of the one endowed with power outwits.
new: [When] the enemy and the conqueror, having combined, two enemies, two attackers of the other, are seizing the heel, he who seizes the heel of one endowed with power outwits.
why: reviewer (minor): Unmarked definite article 'the one' added; Sanskrit has none (cf. unit 3 'of one of large undertaking').

old: For one of large undertaking, having cut off the enemy, can cut off the heel-seizer, not one of small undertaking, with his wheel stuck.
new: For one of large undertaking, having cut off the enemy, can cut off the heel-seizer, not one of small undertaking, with a stuck wheel.
why: reviewer (minor): 'his' is not in the Sanskrit (sakta-cakraḥ is a bahuvrīhi).

old: By that, the seizing of the heel of attackers who are a taker of the base, one of the immediate, a miser is explained.
new: By that, the seizing of the heel of attackers who are takers of the base, [those] of the immediate, misers is explained.
why: reviewer (minor): Singular nouns for a plural genitive compound (abhiyogināṃ); 'one of' is an unmarked addition.

old: In the seizing of the heel of the two attackers of an ally, those alone are the reasons.
new: In the seizing of the heel of the two attackers of an ally, those alone [are] the reasons.
why: reviewer (minor): Verbless clause: copula 'are' must be bracketed in English (as 7.9 '[is] better').

old: treaty
new: peace
why: reviewer (minor): Gloss says 'treaty' but the English text (correctly, bare sandhi = peace) says 'peace'.

old: For peace with an ally is easy to do, not with an enemy.
new: For peace with an ally [is] easy to do, not with an enemy.
why: reviewer (minor): Verbless clause: copula must be bracketed.

old: लाभ पाकर चले जाने पर जिसका शत्रु लाभ से, शक्ति से हीन है, वह पार्ष्णिग्राह छल लेता है, अथवा जिसके लिए जिस पर चढ़ाई करनी है, शत्रु के विग्रह और अपकार में समर्थ हो।
new: लाभ पाकर चले जाने पर जिसका शत्रु लाभ से, शक्ति से हीन है, वह पार्ष्णिग्राह छल लेता है, अथवा जिसका जिस पर चढ़ाई करनी है, शत्रु के विग्रह और अपकार में समर्थ हो।
why: reviewer (minor): 'जिसके लिए' (for whom) is an unmarked change of yasya (genitive 'whose').

old: A weak one standing in the middle of the enemy and the leader is called antardhi; the repulse [is that] of the strong, who has fort, forest and a place of retreat.
new: A weak one standing in the middle of the enemy and the leader is called antardhi; the repulse of the strong [is] possessing fort, forest and a place of retreat.
why: reviewer (minor): 'that' is an interpretive addition inside the bracket and 'who' attaches a nominative (apasāravān) to the genitive balavataḥ; supply only the bare copula.

old: शत्रु और नेता के मध्य में स्थित दुर्बल अन्तर्धि कहा जाता है; बलवान् का प्रतिघात दुर्ग, वन और अपसार वाला है।
new: शत्रु और नेता के मध्य में स्थित दुर्बल अन्तर्धि कहा जाता है; बलवान् का प्रतिघात दुर्ग, वन, अपसार वाला है।
why: reviewer (minor): Three-member dvandva in Hindi takes commas only (glossary 3.15/3.16/7.17).

old: किन्तु शत्रु और विजिगीषु दोनों के, मध्यम को पाना चाहते हुए, मध्यम का पार्ष्णि पकड़ने पर, लाभ पाकर चले जाने पर, जो मध्यम को मित्र से अलग करता है और शत्रु को मित्र के रूप में प्राप्त करता है, वह छल लेता है।
new: किन्तु शत्रु और विजिगीषु दोनों के, मध्यम को पाना चाहते हुए, मध्यम का पार्ष्णि पकड़ने पर, लाभ पाकर चले जाने पर, जो मध्यम को मित्र से अलग करता है और शत्रु को, मित्र को प्राप्त करता है, वह छल लेता है।
why: reviewer (minor): 'के रूप में' (as) is an unmarked addition; Hindi cannot bracket, so leave the double accusative as in the Sanskrit (English keeps '[as]' bracketed).

old: Last clause 'amitraṃ ca mitram āpnoti' is ambiguous (the position of ca; 'obtains the enemy as an ally' is supplied in brackets in English; alternative 'obtains an enemy and an ally'); the Hindi 'के रूप में' follows the English supply. The genitive duals are taken as absolute. tu = but (किन्तु); madhyama = the middle king (glossary 6.2).
new: Last clause 'amitraṃ ca mitram āpnoti' is ambiguous (the position of ca; 'obtains the enemy as an ally' is supplied in brackets in English; alternative 'obtains an enemy and an ally'); the Hindi 'के रूप में' follows the English supply. The genitive duals are taken as absolute. tu = but (किन्तु); madhyama = the middle king (glossary 6.2). Hindi leaves the two accusatives (amitraṃ, mitram) unlinked, with no 'के रूप में', since Hindi cannot bracket a supplied 'as'.
why: reviewer (minor): Note says the Hindi follows the English supply; no longer true after the fix.

old: ally
new: from an ally
why: reviewer (minor): Ablative gloss lacks 'from' (other ablatives: 'from gain').

old: And an enemy who does a favour is one with whom peace is to be made, not an ally who has departed from the state of ally.
new: And an enemy who does a favour is one to be allied with, not an ally who has departed from the state of ally.
why: reviewer (minor): Glossary 7.6 fixes sandheya = to be allied with (सन्धि करने योग्य); align within Book 7.

old: to be made peace with
new: to be allied with

old: sandheya = one with whom peace is to be made (sandhi = peace, glossary 7.3; 'treaty' is the alternative); upakurvāṇa = doing a favour (helping). utkrānta = gone out, departed (alternative 'transgressed').
new: sandheya = one with whom peace is to be made (sandhi = peace, glossary 7.3; 'treaty' is the alternative); upakurvāṇa = doing a favour (helping). utkrānta = gone out, departed (alternative 'transgressed'). Rendered 'to be allied with' per glossary 7.6 (sandheya/asandheya); 'one with whom peace is to be made' is the literal alternative.
why: reviewer (minor): Note should record the 7.6 rendering.

old: “But in [the case of] seizing the heel and marching against, there is a heaping up from war of counsel
new: “But in [the case of] seizing the heel and marching against, [there is] a heaping up from war of counsel

old: dvandva m./n. loc. du.
new: dvandva n. loc. du.
why: reviewer (minor): Both members (grahaṇa, abhiyāna) are neuter; 'm./n.' is wrong.

old: For in war of exertion, by loss and expenditure, there is no growth of the two.
new: For in war of exertion, by loss and expenditure, [there is] no growth of both.
why: reviewer (minor): Verbless clause: bracket the copula; ubhayoḥ = of both.

old: Of the two who first kill the treasonable army also, he who would have killed the more abundant, the more powerful and the utterly treasonable outwits.
new: Of the two who first kill the treasonable army also, he who should cause the more abundant, the more powerful and the utterly treasonable to be killed outwits.
why: reviewer (minor): 'would have killed' reads as a past counterfactual; ghātayet is a causative optative (gloss itself says 'should have killed').

old: जब पार्ष्णिग्राह हो, या आक्रमणकारी हो, या जिस पर चढ़ाई करनी है, ऐसा हो, तब वहाँ विजिगीषु इस नेत्र का आचरण करे।
new: जब पार्ष्णिग्राह, या आक्रमणकारी, या जिस पर चढ़ाई करनी है, हो, तब वहाँ विजिगीषु इस नेत्र का आचरण करे।
why: reviewer (minor): 'ऐसा' and the repeated 'हो' are unmarked additions; bhavet occurs once.

old: आक्रन्द के साथ आक्रमण करता हुआ पार्ष्णिग्राह का निवारण करे; वैसे आक्रन्द की सहायता से पार्ष्णिग्राह की सहायता करने वाले का निवारण करे।
new: आक्रन्द के साथ आक्रमण करता हुआ पार्ष्णिग्राह का निवारण करे; उसी प्रकार आक्रन्द की सहायता से पार्ष्णिग्राह की सहायता करने वाले का निवारण करे।

old: And with the enemy's ally he should obstruct the ally in front; the ally's ally, and also of the enemy, he should keep off with the ally's ally.
new: And with the enemy's ally he should jostle the ally in front; the ally's ally, and also of the enemy, he should keep off with the ally's ally.

old: और शत्रु के मित्र से मित्र को सामने बाधित करे; मित्र के मित्र को, और शत्रु के भी, मित्र के मित्र से निवारण करे।

old: should obstruct

old: Obscure. avaghaṭṭayet is literally 'cause to rub against, jostle'; rendered 'obstruct'. ari-mitra = ally of the enemy (alternative: some other relation); the object in line a is simply 'ally' (whose ally is not stated). Line b is elliptical ('and of the enemy also' = the enemy's ally's ally); read as given, with ca and api both rendered.
new: Obscure. avaghaṭṭayet is literally 'cause to rub against, jostle'; rendered 'obstruct'. ari-mitra = ally of the enemy (alternative: some other relation); the object in line a is simply 'ally' (whose ally is not stated). Line b is elliptical ('and of the enemy also' = the enemy's ally's ally); read as given, with ca and api both rendered. 'obstruct' withdrawn at review: avaghaṭṭayet is kept literal ('jostle'); the actual sense is unsettled. The '.' joins in ari.mitreṇa and mitra.mitram(-eṇa) are genuine compounds (enemy's ally, ally's ally), one w entry each: checked, correct.
why: reviewer (minor): Record the withdrawal.

old: इस प्रकार विजिगीषु स्वयं के लिए मण्डल की स्थापना करे, पीछे और आगे, मित्र प्रकृति की सम्पत्ति से।
